chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
There has never been, nor will there be until the Hour is established, any believer except that he has a neighbor who harms him.

key_terms.السَّاعَةُ: the Hour, meaning the Day of Judgment
key_terms.جَارٌ: a neighbor, the one living nearby in social proximity
key_terms.مُؤْمِنٌ: a believer, one characterized by faith
key_terms.يُؤْذِيهِ: harms him or causes him distress

ai.seo_question: Does every believer face harm or difficulty from neighbors?
ai.summary: This hadith states that hardship from neighbors is an enduring reality in the life of the believer. It highlights patience as part of the believer’s covenant and frames social harm as a recurring trial that accompanies faith until the Day of Judgment.
